decisions.executionNote: Begin a gradual elbow-up approach with the left arm toward the purple nut; keep the right arm parked. Initial lift and wrist reorientation use small increments for configuration continuity.
Complete the left elbow-up wrist-down approach and move above the purple nut estimated from the calibrated head image. Stop above grasp height for wrist alignment.
Correct the purple-nut approach for the lower tabletop inferred from the views, descend to grasp height, close fully, and lift to check retention.
Correct the rejected tensor; no preceding motion occurred. Carry the retained purple nut to its screw and lower toward engagement, with the right arm stationary.
Fine-align the purple nut from the wrist view, lower a few millimeters, and begin a slow clockwise threading turn. Engagement remains visually uncertain.
Continue clockwise threading of the purple pair, then open and begin resetting the wrist without reversing the nut.
The purple screw cap now appears flush in its nut. Release and lift clear, then approach the gray nut near the center with the left arm for a staged handover.
Descend onto the gray nut, close fully, then lift a short distance to inspect retention before moving it to the center handover location.
Gray nut is visibly retained. Place it upright at the center for a non-crossing handover, release, and lift the left gripper clear.
Withdraw left toward the yellow nut while the right arm starts a slow elbow-up approach toward the staged gray nut. Maintain lateral separation.
Use the calibrated tabletop estimate to grasp and test-lift the yellow nut with left. Complete the right wrist-down approach and translate toward the staged gray nut, remaining above it.
Yellow nut is visibly retained; lift and hold it in the left workspace. Move the right gripper over the staged gray nut and descend to its grasp height, keeping the arms separated.
Fine-center the right gripper on the staged gray nut, close fully, lift, and begin moving it into the right workspace. Left holds the yellow nut clear of the handover area.
Carry the retained gray nut over its screw and lower to initial engagement height. Meanwhile stage the yellow nut at the center for the next handover, maintaining arm separation.
Set down and release the yellow nut, then withdraw left. Fine-align and lower the gray nut, beginning a slow clockwise threading stroke with the right gripper closed.
Gray screw cap appears seated flush in the nut. Release and lift right, reset its wrist while approaching the staged yellow nut. Begin returning the empty left arm along an elevated, continuous path.
Pick up the staged yellow nut with the right gripper and test-lift it. Complete the empty left arm's gradual return toward its original pose.
Yellow nut is retained. Lift it above the other hardware and carry it over the matching yellow screw in the right workspace; keep the left arm at its returned pose.
Lower the yellow nut toward its screw with a small lateral correction from the head view. Pause at initial engagement height to inspect concentric alignment before turning.
Make a small wrist-view centering correction, lower the yellow nut to engagement, and begin a gentle clockwise threading stroke. Keep the left arm parked and both configurations continuous.
The yellow nut appears tilted rather than seated. Stop turning and lift gently to clear the screw and reassess alignment while keeping the gripper closed.
The yellow nut remains tilted in the grip after clearing the screw. Move it to a clear patch in the right workspace for a controlled set-down and upright regrasp.
Set the yellow nut down gently and open the right gripper, allowing it to settle before lifting clear to inspect its orientation.
The yellow nut has settled upright. Recenter over its new position, square the gripper axis vertically, descend for a fresh grasp, and lift slightly to verify retention.
The last grasp missed; the nut remains on the table. Open, lift clear, and correct toward the nut using the wrist-image offset, then inspect alignment before closing again.
Continue the observed wrist-image correction to place the upright yellow nut between the fingers, descend slightly, close, and make a short retention-check lift.
The fingers closed above the yellow nut rather than retaining it. Reopen, descend at the now-centered location to reach the nut sides, and perform another short grasp-and-lift check.
Reopen and correct the lateral overshoot using the head view rather than the height-dependent wrist offset. Descend open at the revised yellow-nut location and inspect before closing.
At grasp height, make a small two-axis correction to center the yellow nut in the open fingers. Close fully and lift slowly to verify an upright retained grasp.
The yellow nut is now visibly retained. Lift clear and transfer it toward the yellow screw using the observed nut-to-screw displacement, then stop near engagement for another alignment check.
The yellow screw tip is visible within the nut bore. Make a millimeter-scale centering and seating correction, then apply a short slow clockwise threading stroke while watching for tilt.
The yellow screw tip is now concentric in the nut. Continue a short clockwise stroke with slight downward following, then open and reset the wrist within its rotation margin.

Reset the open right wrist for another tightening stroke and make a small centering correction toward the yellow nut. The screw remains in the bore, but visible threads indicate more seating is needed.
Center the open fingers more closely on the yellow nut, regrasp its sides, and apply another controlled clockwise tightening stroke with small downward following.
Continue the yellow nut's clockwise tightening stroke, keeping the grip closed and following downward slowly. Stop short of the wrist rotation limit for another reset if needed.
Open the right gripper and reset its wrist for a longer tightening stroke, without lifting or reversing the seated nut. Keep the current height while assessing thread depth.
Regrasp the yellow nut and apply a longer, controlled clockwise stroke. Use only slight vertical following to avoid forcing the threads; keep both arms in their current elbow-up branches.
Finish this short yellow tightening stroke at constant height, then release and reset the wrist while keeping the nut seated and avoiding the joint limit.
Regrasp and apply another moderate clockwise tightening stroke to the seated yellow pair, then open for an unobstructed retention and seating check.
The yellow nut remains seated after release. Lift clear with the gripper open and reset the right wrist at a safe height before returning it to origin.
All three color-matched pairs remain together, with screw caps visible in the nuts. Begin a gradual elevated right-arm return and remove the small left-origin residual, keeping both grippers open.
Complete the right arm's smooth return to its original pose while holding both grippers open. The three assembled pairs remain undisturbed on the table.
